consumer: The dialogue/condition u_has_item/npc_has_item lambda built by conditional_t::set_has_item, which asks 'does this actor possess item X' and EVALUATES a yes/no a mission or dialogue check consumes.
scope: only the character's own carried items (on-person possession: inventory/worn/wielded as seen by charges_of and has_amount), not nearby reachable items and not a map region
decisive_source: src/condition.cpp::conditional_t<T>::set_has_item — its body returns actor->charges_of(item_id) > 0 || actor->has_amount(item_id, 1), the engine's own computed possession predicate over the character actor, which is the authority a mission/dialogue check reads.
divergence: Avatar carries item X only as charges inside a container (count_by_charges, e.g. 5 charges of a fuel/liquid stored under its container, or ammo inside a magazine): the engine predicate charges_of/has_amount returns TRUE, but a re-derivation from the avatar.carried_items[] snapshot (write_carried_items) or a visit_items traversal that skips gun/magazine contents (visit_internal) reports no carried_items entry with type_id==X, yielding a wrong NO.
